messages:
maya (oncall): incident-bot fired for high kv-cache miss+eviction rate in ntk/rope-serving cluster. dashboards show >15x eviction rate starting ~1872003000. paging the oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: kv-cache-eviction-spike (sev2). Runbook: check batching, prefetch, and sliding-window configs.
maya (oncall): i'm on it. first quick check — any deploys in the last 30m? @deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: No production deployments recorded in last 60m for rope-serving. Canary jobs show increase in avg seqlen for a subset of requests.
arjun (runtime): seeing heavy continuous-batch queue growth on nodes serving longctx workers. latency p95 from 120ms -> 2.3s on those shards. logs show repeated KV key churn: keys created for sliding-window prefixes, TTLs not expiring fast enough.
sarah (sre): QPS overall steady but headroom exhausted on kv servers. eviction storms causing CPU spikes and packet drops. network errors to redis-cluster-like store rising.
alex (ml): we rolled NTK-aware sliding-window + YaRN affinity in the last week to handle long-context token-keying. hypothesis: YaRN affinity increased key cardinality when sequence-length distribution spiked -> eviction.
maya (oncall): good theory. mitigation plan — we should: 1) disable sliding-window prefetch on affected pool, 2) throttle continuous-batch, 3) increase TTL aggressive eviction policy as temporary. who can apply hotpatch?
arjun (runtime): i can hotpatch the batcher config. prepping a conservative change: set max_continuous_batch_size=64 -> 32 and reduce prefetch_window=2048 -> 512 for pool rope-longctx-1.
maya (oncall): do it. patch and report. i'll notify customers. :raising_hand:
arjun (runtime): applying change now. kubectl patch configmap rope-batcher --patch '{"data":{"max_batch_sz":"32","prefetch_window":"512"}}' --namespace=prod
deploy-bot: Patch applied to configmap rope-batcher in prod. Rolling restart of batcher pods started (gradual to avoid cold-start).
arjun (runtime): rollout in progress. watching queues.
(5m later)
arjun (runtime): queue lengths dropping. eviction rate down from 15x -> ~2x baseline. CPU normalizing. p95 latency improving.
sarah (sre): monitoring kernel and redis metrics. connections stabilized. No more packet drops.
maya (oncall): maya -> handoff to sarah in 30m. full incident doc later. who owned the customer comms?
customer-success: i've drafted a short note for impacted customers: "We observed transient increased latency for some long-context requests due to a cache churn issue after rolling NTK/YaRN affinity. We implemented a targeted performance hotpatch (reduced prefetch + smaller batch size) and are monitoring improvements. No data loss. Reprocessing not required." want to send after we confirm stability.
alex (ml): followup: need to refine YaRN affinity heuristics so high-cardinality prefixes don't amplify key domain. suggestion: add cardinality threshold and fallback to static routing for extreme seqlen spikes. I'll open RFC ticket.
arjun (runtime): logging shows a handful of high-ntk requesters (bots/streams) responsible for ~70% of new keys. we should add requester-level rate limiting in front of prefetch.
devex: also want to surface a dev-tooling flag to emulate YaRN on short dev clusters to catch this earlier.
maya (oncall): good action items: (1) sarah to own monitoring & postmortem, (2) arjun to revert hotpatch when safe and prepare a tested rollout with autoslowdown, (3) alex to RFC YaRN safeguards, (4) cs to send customer note after 1h stability.
sarah (sre): acknowledged. starting incident timeline capture now. will include exact impacted percentage: preliminary estimate ~4.7% of production requests experienced >1s extra latency, errors stayed <0.2% overall.
maya (oncall): marking page resolved for now, keeping channel open for followups. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated. Followup: schedule postmortem and tag owners: sarah, arjun, alex, customer-success.
(end thread)
